Y Chromosome: Fewest genes (231).
explanation: Chromosome 1 completion marked the final chapter of human euchromatin sequencing.
SNPs ("snips") occur at ~1.4 million locations in the human genome. Valuable for tracing human history, disease susceptibility, and personalized medicine.

Invented by Alec Jeffreys using VNTRs (Variable Number of Tandem Repeats) as radiolabeled probes. Steps: DNA Isolation → Restriction Digestion → Gel Electrophoresis → Southern Blotting → Hybridization with VNTR → Autoradiography.

bullets: 20 BYA: Big Bang (Universe)
4.5 BYA: Formation of Earth
4.0 BYA: Origin of Life
3.5 BYA: First non-cellular life
explanation: Crucial timeline figures (BYA = Billion Years Ago) frequently asked in NEET matching questions.

mnemonic: in Primitive Earth's Atmosphere 	C-M-A-W (NO OXYGEN)
explanation: Carbon dioxide / Methane (CH4) • Ammonia (NH3) • Water vapour (H2O) Primitive atmosphere was strictly reducing because free molecular oxygen (O2) was completely absent.

bullets: Temperature: 800°C
Gas mixture: CH4 + NH3 + H2O + H2 (Spark discharge using electrodes)
explanation: SL Miller (1953) simulated chemical evolution in laboratory conditions as proposed by Oparin & Haldane.

mnemonic: Synthesized in Miller's Experiment 	AMINO ACIDS (A-G-A)
explanation: Formed Amino acids (specifically Alanine, Glycine, Aspartic acid) along with organic acids and sugars. Analysis of meteorite content also revealed similar amino acids, proving cosmic universality of chemical evolution.

mnemonic: of Origin of Life 	P - S - C - C
explanation: Panspermia (Spore theory) • Spontaneous generation (Abiogenesis) • Catastrophism • Chemical evolution Louis Pasteur experimentally disproved Spontaneous Generation using swan-necked flash experiment.
Life arose from pre-existing non-living organic molecules (abiotic chemical evolution preceded biogenesis). Oparin (Russia) and Haldane (England) proposed that life originated in a warm dilute soup.

mnemonic: Non-Cellular vs Cellular Forms 	3 BYA (RNA/PROTEIN) vs 2 BYA (SINGLE CELL)
bullets: 3 BYA: Non-cellular macromolecular aggregates (RNA, Proteins, Polysaccharides).
2 BYA: First cellular forms of life.
explanation: First cellular forms were unicellular heterotrophs originating in aquatic environment.

mnemonic: Melanism (Biston betularia) 	WHITE = PRE-IND / DARK = POST-IND
bullets: Before 1850s (Pre-industrial): White-winged moth survived (lichens on trees).
After 1850s (Post-industrial): Melanic/Dark moth survived (soot covered trees).
explanation: Classic NCERT example demonstrating Natural Selection in response to environmental change.

Resistant varieties evolved due to human action: Pesticides resistance • Herbicides resistance • Drug-resistant microbes Proves that evolution is a stochastic process based on chance events in nature and mutation.

mnemonic: Radiation Definition 	SINGLE POINT TO OTHER HABITATS
explanation: Evolutionary process where species evolve from a common ancestral point and radiate into different geographical areas. Driven by natural selection exploiting unoccupied ecological niches.

mnemonic: Structures (Divergent Evolution) 	HD - SAME ORIGIN, DIFFERENT FUNCTION
explanation: Homology leads to Divergent Evolution. Same basic anatomical origin/structure, modified for different functions. Indicates common ancestry among differing species groups.

bullets: Animals: Forelimbs of Whales, Bats, Cheetahs, and Humans.
Plants: Thorns of Bougainvillea and Tendrils of Cucurbita.
explanation: Both plant structures arise from axillary position despite serving protection vs climbing roles.

mnemonic: Structures (Convergent Evolution) 	AC - DIFFERENT ORIGIN, SAME FUNCTION
explanation: Analogy leads to Convergent Evolution. Different origin and internal anatomy, selected for similar ecological functions. Result of similar adaptation to convergent selection pressures in similar environments.

mnemonic: of Analogous Organs 	WINGS - EYES - FLIPPERS - TUBERS
bullets: Wings of Butterfly and Birds
Eyes of Octopus and Mammals
Flippers of Penguins and Dolphins
Sweet Potato (root modification) and Potato (stem modification)
explanation: Four core NCERT examples indispensable for NEET assertion-reason questions.

bullets: Galapagos Finches: Beak shape adapted from seed-eating to insectivorous/vegetarian.
Australian Marsupials: Radiated from single ancestor within isolated continent.
explanation: Adaptive radiation occurs within a single isolated geographical area.

mnemonic: Evolution in Marsupials vs Placentals 	MARSUPIAL = PLACENTAL PAIRS
bullets: Tasmanian Wolf ↔ Anteater / Wolf
Sugar Glider ↔ Flying Squirrel
Marsupial Mole ↔ Mole
Banded Anteater ↔ Numbat
explanation: When more than one adaptive radiation occurs in an isolated region, it represents convergent evolution.

mnemonic: Evidence for Evolution 	PROTEINS & GENES SIMILARITY
explanation: Similarities in proteins, enzymes, and blood plasma perform functions across diverse organisms. Biochemical similarity points toward shared ancestral lineage at molecular level.

Haeckel proposed that embryonic development repeats adult evolutionary history (e.g., vestigial gill slits in human embryos). Theory completely disproved by Karl Ernst von Baer (noted embryos never pass through adult stages of other animals).
Different aged rock strata contain fossils showing life forms restricted to specific geological eras. Fossil records directly prove that life forms have changed over long geological time periods.

mnemonic: Theory of Evolution 	USE & DISUSE OF ORGANS
explanation: Evolution driven by use and disuse of organs + inheritance of acquired characteristics (e.g., Giraffe neck elongation). Disproved as acquired somatic characters are not transferred to germline cells.

mnemonic: Concepts of Darwinian Theory 	BRANCHING DESCENT & NATURAL SELECTION
bullets: Branching Descent: Explains adaptive diversification.
Natural Selection: Fitness based on reproductive capability.
explanation: Alfred Russel Wallace reached similar conclusions working in Malay Archipelago.

mnemonic: de Vries Mutation Theory 	SALTATION = SINGLE STEP LARGE MUTATION
explanation: Based on Oenothera lamarckiana (Evening Primrose); proposed evolution is discontinuous and directional-less. Darwinian variations are small & directional; De Vriesian mutations are random & directionless.

bullets: p: Frequency of dominant allele (A)
q: Frequency of recessive allele (a)
p²: AA Homozygous dominant • 2pq: Aa Heterozygous • q²: aa Homozygous recessive
explanation: Allele frequencies in a stable population remain constant generation to generation if undisturbed.

mnemonic: Affecting Hardy-Weinberg Equilibrium 	G - G - M - R - N
explanation: Gene Migration • Genetic Drift • Mutation • Recombination • Natural Selection Disturbance in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium indicates evolutionary change is occurring.

mnemonic: Drift vs Founder Effect 	SMALL POPULATION CHANCE EVENT
bullets: Genetic Drift: Random change in gene frequencies occurring purely by chance.
Founder Effect: Original drifted population forms new colony becoming distinct species.
explanation: Operates prominently in small isolated populations.

mnemonic: of Natural Selection Curves 	S - D - D
bullets: Stabilizing: Peak gets higher/narrower (favors mean phenotype).
Directional: Peak shifts in one direction.
Disruptive: Two peaks form (favors extreme phenotypes).
explanation: Critical curve diagram-based question topic in NCERT textbook.
Caught in South Africa in 1938; Lobefins were ancestors of modern amphibians. Thought to be extinct; crucial transitional evolutionary bridge between fishes and amphibians.

mnemonic: Land Vertebrates & Reptiles 	AMPHIBIANS → REPTILES (SHELL EGGS)
explanation: Amphibians invaded land first; evolved into Reptiles laying thick-shelled eggs that don't dry in sun. Allowed complete independence from aquatic breeding environments.
Some land reptiles went back into water to evolve into fish-like reptiles around 200 MYA. Example of secondary adaptation to aquatic life.
Largest dinosaur (~20 feet height) with fearsome dagger-like teeth; extinct ~65 MYA. Dinosaurs suddenly disappeared 65 MYA (Cretaceous-Tertiary extinction).

mnemonic: Eras Chronology 	P - M - C (PAST TO PRESENT)
explanation: Palaeozoic → Mesozoic → Cenozoic Era Cenozoic is Era of Mammals/Birds; Mesozoic is Era of Reptiles/Dinosaurs; Palaeozoic is Era of Invertebrates/Early Fishes.

mnemonic: Periods Order 	C - O - S - D - C - P
explanation: Cambrian • Ordovician • Silurian • Devonian • Carboniferous • Permian Devonian is Age of Fishes; Carboniferous is Age of Amphibians & Coal Forests.
Triassic • Jurasic • Cretaceous Jurassic was dominated by Dinosaurs and Gymnosperms.
Green algae (Chlorophyte ancestor) → Tracheophyte ancestors → Rhynia-type plants. Rhynia-type plants directly gave rise to Psilophyton, ancestral to modern vascular plants.

bullets: Pteridophytes (Ferns)
Conifers / Gymnosperms
Seed ferns (Gave rise to Angiosperms)
explanation: Psilophyton gave rise to: Key central ancestral node in NCERT plant evolutionary tree.

bullets: Sauropsids: Gave rise to Lizards, Snakes, Turtles, Dinosaurs, Birds.
Synapsids: Gave rise to Pelycosaurs, Therapsids, Mammals.
explanation: Mammals originated from Synapsid lineage, NOT from dinosaurs.
First mammals were small, shrew-like creatures whose fossils were small sized. Mammals were viviparous, intelligent, and protected unborn young inside mother's body.

mnemonic: Drift Impact on Mammals 	AUSTRALIAN MARSUPIAL SURVIVAL
explanation: Australia severed from main landmass; Pouched marsupials survived due to lack of competition from placentals. Geographical isolation preserved unique fauna in Australia.

mnemonic: History of Horse 	E - M - M - P - E
explanation: Eohippus → Mesohippus → Merychippus → Pliohippus → Equus (Modern Horse) Structural progression involved reduction of digits and elongation of limbs for running.
Whales, Dolphins, Seals, and Sea cows evolved stream-lined bodies for aquatic mode of life. Placental mammals secondary return to water showing convergent aquatic adaptations.

mnemonic: Evolution Order Mnemonic DR. RAMA'S AUSTRALIAN HOMINID ERECTS NEANDERTHAL SAPIENS
explanation: Dryopithecus → Ramapithecus → Australopithecus → Habilis → Erectus → Neanderthal → Sapiens Flawless chronological sequence for NEET questions.

mnemonic: vs Ramapithecus 	DRY = APE-LIKE / RAMA = MAN-LIKE
bullets: Dryopithecus: More ape-like, hairy, walked like gorillas.
Ramapithecus: More man-like.
explanation: Existed 15 MYA. Fossils found in Shivalik hills in India and East Africa.

mnemonic: habilis (First Hominid) 	650-800 CC & DID NOT EAT MEAT
bullets: Brain capacity: 650–800 cc
First human-like hominid feature
Did NOT eat meat (vegetarian tool maker)
explanation: Called "handy man" because they crafted basic chipped stone tools.

mnemonic: Man Features 	1400 CC - HIDES - BURIED DEAD
bullets: Capacity: 1400 cc • Used animal hides to protect body • Buried their dead
explanation: Lived in East & Central Asia (1,00,000–40,000 years ago). High intellectual level and cultural practices recorded.

mnemonic: sapiens Origin & Ice Age 	AFRICA - ICE AGE (75,000-10,000 YRS)
explanation: Arose in Africa; moved across continents during Ice Age (75,000–10,000 years ago). Pre-historic cave art developed around 18,000 years ago (Bhimbetka caves in MP).

bullets: Homo habilis: 650–800 cc
Homo erectus: 900 cc
Neanderthal: 1400 cc
Homo sapiens: 1350–1400 cc
explanation: Cranial capacity growth reflects progressive cerebral cortex evolution.

mnemonic: of Evolutionary Milestones 	INVERTEBRATES (500) - JAWLESS (350) - LAND (320)
bullets: 500 MYA: Invertebrates formed
350 MYA: Jawless fish
320 MYA: Sea weeds & plants on land
explanation: Complete NCERT quantitative timeline summary for quick revision before exam.

explanation: Typhoid (Salmonella typhi) • Tetanus (Clostridium tetani) • Pneumonia (Streptococcus) • Syphilis • Diphtheria Bacterial pathogens cause severe systemic infections; S. typhi targets small intestine, S. pneumoniae infects lung alveoli.

bullets: S: Sustained high fever (39°C–40°C)
T: Typhoid Mary (Mary Mallon) carrier • O: Organ perforation in severe cases

mnemonic: Pathogenesis & Symptoms 	F - L - U - I - D

mnemonic: Cold vs Pneumonia Distinction 	C - O - L - D
bullets: C: Caused by Rhinoviruses
O: Organs: Nose & respiratory passage, BUT NOT lungs
L: Lasts 3 to 7 days
D: Droplet infection via contaminated pens, books, cups

explanation: Transmitted via drinking water and food contaminated by fecal matter through houseflies.

mnemonic: Species Causing Malaria 	P - V - M - O - F
explanation: P. vivax • P. malariae • P. ovale • P. falciparum Malignant malaria caused by P. falciparum is the most serious and can be fatal.

mnemonic: Life Cycle: Human Stage 	S - L - R - T

L: Liver cells target: Parasite multiplies asexually in liver
R: Red Blood Cells attack: Parasite multiplies in RBCs causing rupture
T: Toxic Hemozoin released causing recurring fever every 3–4 days
explanation: Rupture of RBCs releases toxin Hemozoin, responsible for periodic chills and high fever.

bullets: G: Gametocytes taken up by female Anopheles from human blood
F: Fertilization & development occur in mosquito gut
S: Sporozoites formed and escape gut to migrate
S: Stored in Salivary glands ready for next host bite

mnemonic: Parasites (Ascaris & Wuchereria) 	A - S - C - W - U

explanation: Microsporum • Epidermophyton • Trichophyton These three genera are responsible for ringworm, one of the most common infectious diseases in humans.

mnemonic: Symptoms & Favorable Conditions 	D - R - Y - H
bullets: D: Dry, scaly lesions on skin, nails, and scalp
R: Redness accompanied by intense itching
Y: Yielded/favored by heat and moisture in skin folds (groin, toes)
H: Hygiene lack: Transmitted via towels, clothes, combs
explanation: Heat and moisture help these fungi grow, making skin folds prime sites for infection.

mnemonic: Control of Mosquito Vectors 	G - D
bullets: Gambusia: Fish introduced into water bodies that feeds on mosquito larvae
Dragonflies: Predators that feed on adult mosquitoes
explanation: Ecological control measure introduced in ponds and tanks to eliminate mosquito breeding.

mnemonic: & Public Hygiene Measures 	C - L - E - A - N
bullets: C: Clean body maintenance • L: Liquid/food hygiene (clean drinking water)
E: Excreta and waste proper disposal • A: Air hygiene (avoid overcrowding)
N: Neat surroundings: Periodic cleaning of water reservoirs and coolers
explanation: Essential for controlling infectious diseases, especially water-borne pathogens like S. typhi and E. histolytica.

mnemonic: Mosquito Vector Features 	A - E - D - E - S
bullets: A: Aedes aegypti vector • E: Epidemic vector for Dengue & Chikungunya
D: Day-time biting preference • E: Elimination of stagnant water stops breeding
S: Symptoms: High fever, joint pain, platelet drop (Dengue)
explanation: Controlling stagnant water in coolers and rooftops directly suppresses Aedes population.

mnemonic: Immunity Barriers 	P - P - C - C
bullets: Physical: Skin, Mucus coating of respiratory, gastrointestinal & urogenital tracts
Physiological: Acid in stomach, Saliva in mouth, Tears from eyes (lysozyme)
Cellular: PMNL-neutrophils, Monocytes, Natural Killer cells, Macrophages
Cytokine: Interferons produced by virus-infected cells
explanation: Innate immunity provides non-specific defense present from birth through four distinct barriers.

mnemonic: Barriers of Innate Immunity 	P - M - N - K - M
bullets: PMNL: Polymorpho-nuclear Leukocytes (Neutrophils)
Monocytes: Phagocytic blood cells • NK: Natural Killer lymphocytes
Macrophages: Phagocytic cells in tissues
explanation: These cells phagocytose and destroy invading microbes non-specifically.

mnemonic: Barrier (Interferons) 	V - I - R - U - S
bullets: V: Virus-infected cells produce proteins called Interferons
I: Interferons protect non-infected surrounding cells
R: Resistance to viral replication induced in healthy cells
U: Uninfected cell shield • S: Secreted glycoproteins
explanation: Interferons form a chemical shield that prevents viral replication in neighboring healthy cells.

mnemonic: of Acquired Immunity 	M - S - D - A
bullets: M: Memory: Heightened secondary response upon re-exposure
S: Specificity for individual antigens
D: Discrimination between Self and Non-self
A: Antigen-driven response mediated by B & T lymphocytes
explanation: Acquired immunity is pathogen-specific and characterized by immunological memory.

bullets: H₂: Two Heavy polypeptide chains
L₂: Two Light polypeptide chains held together by disulfide bonds
explanation: Each antibody molecule has 4 peptide chains represented as H ₂L ₂; forms Y-shaped structure.

mnemonic: Classes of Immunoglobulins 	M - A - G - E - D
bullets: IgM: First responder, pentameric • IgA: Secretions (Colostrum, tears, saliva)
IgG: Most abundant, crosses placenta • IgE: Allergies & parasite defense
IgD: B-cell surface receptor
explanation: IgG is the only antibody that crosses the placenta; IgA provides mucosal protection.

mnemonic: vs Cell-Mediated Immunity (CMI) 	H - B - C - T
bullets: H: Humoral immunity mediated by antibodies in body fluids (humors)
B: B-lymphocytes produce antibodies
C: Cell-mediated immunity (CMI) mediated by T-lymphocytes
T: T-cells responsible for graft rejection in organ transplants
explanation: T-cells do not secrete antibodies themselves but help B-cells produce them and execute CMI.

mnemonic: Rejection & Organ Transplantation 	T - M - I - S
bullets: T: T-lymphocytes mediate Graft Rejection via CMI
M: Matching required: Tissue matching & Blood group matching
I: Immunosuppressants (e.g., Cyclosporin A) required for life
S: Self vs Non-self recognition causes host defense to attack foreign organ
explanation: The body's ability to differentiate self and non-self cells drives graft rejection.

mnemonic: vs Passive Immunity 	A - S - P - R
bullets: A: Active: Host produces own antibodies when exposed to antigen (slow, long-lasting)
S: Slow development of active immunity
P: Passive: Readymade antibodies directly injected/transferred (fast, short-term)
R: Readymade protection (e.g., ATS, Anti-venom, Colostrum IgA)
explanation: Injections against snakebite contain preformed antibodies (passive immunization).

mnemonic: & Infant Protection 	C - A - R - E
bullets: C: Colostrum: Yellowish fluid secreted by mother during early lactation
A: Abundant IgA antibodies present
R: Readymade passive immunity conferred to newborn
E: Essential protection for infant against various pathogens
explanation: Classic example of natural passive immunity in early human development.

mnemonic: & Recombinant Vaccines 	M - E - M - O - R - Y
bullets: M: Memory B & T cells generated upon vaccination
E: Epitopes/Inactivated pathogens introduced safely
M: Massive antibody production upon real pathogen exposure
O: Overwhelms invader rapidly • R: Recombinant DNA tech (e.g., Hepatitis-B vaccine produced in yeast)
Y: Yields long-term protection
explanation: Recombinant DNA technology allows large-scale production of antigenic polypeptides in yeast or bacteria.

mnemonic: & Mast Cell Mediators 	A - L - L - E - R - G - Y
bullets: A: Exaggerated immune response to allergens • L: IgE antibodies produced
L: Release of Histamine & Serotonin from Mast cells
E: Examples: Pollen, mites, animal dander • R: Relieved by Anti-histamines, Adrenaline, Steroids
G: Granules of mast cells rupture • Y: Symptoms: Sneezing, watery eyes, running nose
explanation: Drugs like antihistamine, adrenaline, and steroids quickly reduce allergy symptoms.

mnemonic: of Cancer Cells 	L - O - S - S
bullets: L: Loss of contact inhibition (normal cells stop dividing upon contact; cancer cells lose this)
O: On-going uncontrolled cell division forming mass tumors
S: Structural invasion of surrounding healthy tissues
S: Unchecked proliferation forming neoplastic cells
explanation: Contact inhibition is the property of normal cells that prevents uncontrolled proliferation.

mnemonic: vs Malignant Tumors & Metastasis 	B-C vs M-M
bullets: Benign (B-C): Confined to original location, causes little damage
Malignant (M-M): Mass of proliferating neoplastic cells
Metastasis: Cancer cells slough off, travel via blood, and start new tumors in distant organs
explanation: Metastasis is the most feared property of malignant tumors.

mnemonic: Physical, Chemical & Biological 	P - C - B
bullets: Physical: Ionizing (X-rays, gamma rays) & non-ionizing (UV) radiation
Chemical: Tobacco smoke chemicals (major cause of lung cancer)
Biological: Oncogenic viruses with viral oncogenes (v-onc) / cellular proto-oncogenes (c-onc)
explanation: Proto-oncogenes in normal cells get activated under carcinogen exposure to transform into active oncogenes.

mnemonic: Detection & Diagnostic Techniques 	B - H - M - C - R
bullets: B: Biopsy & histopathological studies • H: Histological tissue staining
M: MRI using non-ionizing radiation & strong magnetic fields
C: Computed Tomography (CT) using X-rays for 3D imagery
R: Radiography & Antibodies against cancer-specific antigens
explanation: MRI generates 3D images of internal soft tissues without harmful ionizing radiation.

mnemonic: Treatment Modalities 	S - R - I - C
bullets: S: Surgery: Physical removal of localized tumor
R: Radiotherapy: Lethal irradiation of tumor cells saving normal tissue
I: Immunotherapy: α-interferon biological response modifier activates immune system
C: Chemotherapy: Anti-cancer drugs (side effects: hair loss, anemia)
explanation: α-interferon is given to cancer patients as it activates their immune system to destroy tumors.

mnemonic: Structure & Genome Characteristics 	R - E - T - R - O
bullets: R: Retrovirus group with single-stranded RNA genome enclosed in envelope
E: Enveloped virus with protein coat
T: Reverse Transcriptase converts viral RNA to viral DNA
R: Reduces CD4 Helper T-lymphocyte count drastically
O: Opportunistic infections occur due to immunodeficiency
explanation: HIV selectively infects and destroys Helper T-lymphocytes (TH cells).

mnemonic: of HIV Transmission 	S - B - N - M
bullets: S: Sexual contact with infected person
B: Transfusion of contaminated Blood and blood products
N: Sharing infected Needles among IV drug abusers
M: Transplacental transfer from infected Mother to child
explanation: HIV does NOT spread by touch, physical contact, or casual hugging; only through body fluids.

mnemonic: Replication & Macrophage Factory 	M - R - I - H
bullets: M: Macrophages act as HIV factory (continuously produce viral particles)
R: Reverse transcriptase synthesizes viral DNA from RNA
I: Integration of viral DNA into host cell genome
H: Helper T-cells invaded and destroyed, lowering immunity
explanation: Macrophages survive HIV infection and act as a persistent HIV factory in the host body.

mnemonic: Source & Action 	P - O - P - S

O: Opioid receptors in Central Nervous System & Gastrointestinal tract

S: Slows down body functions (Depressant)
explanation: Morphine is a highly effective sedative and painkiller given to post-surgery patients.

A: Absence of color/odor: White, odorless, bitter crystalline compound

mnemonic: Source & Organ System 	C - A - N - N - A

A: Affects Cardiovascular system of the body
N: Natural cannabinoids interact with receptors in brain
N: Named products: Marijuana, Hashish, Charas, Ganja

mnemonic: Alkaloid (Cocaine) Mechanism 	C - O - C - A

O: Overdose causes severe Hallucinations
C: CNS stimulant interfering with transport of Dopamine

bullets: Atropa: Atropa belladonna
Datura: Datura species containing tropane alkaloids
Cannabis / LSD: Cannabis sativa (high dose) & LSD (from Claviceps purpurea fungus)

mnemonic: Abused by Addicts 	B - A - M
bullets: B: Barbiturates (Sedatives/hypnotics) • A: Amphetamines (Stimulants)
M: Benzodiazepines (Tranquilizers for anxiety and insomnia)

mnemonic: & Nicotine Health Hazards 	N - I - C - O - T

I: Increases blood pressure and heart rate via Adrenaline
C: CO in smoke reduces oxygen capacity by binding hemoglobin
O: Oncogenic: Causes lung, urinary bladder, and oral cancer

bullets: P: Peer pressure and social acceptance desire

E: Escape from academic stress, pressure, and failure
